skill.name: skill-rails-upgrade
skill.description: Assess Rails applications for version upgrades and guide selective configuration merges.
skill.summary: Plan Rails upgrades with version checks, dependency review, and selective file merge guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The skill is a Rails upgrade workflow that uses public documentation, version checks, and local project inspection. I confirmed the findings where the skill instructs assistants to run CLI, dependency, generator, migration, server, and test commands. Most Markdown backticks, file names, URLs, and /dev/null redirects are false positives, and no prompt injection or malicious exfiltration was found.

remediation.issue: External command execution during upgrade assessment
remediation.suggestion: Gate every shell command behind explicit user approval and show the command, working directory, and expected side effects first.

remediation.issue: Mutating Rails and dependency update steps
remediation.suggestion: Separate assessment from execution, and require a clean git state before bundle updates, npm updates, migrations, generators, or file deletion.

remediation.issue: Network lookups for public release data
remediation.suggestion: Document that the skill may query GitHub, Rails guides, railsdiff.org, and npm for version information.
Update the skill metadata to reflect external command, filesystem, and network activity.

static_findings.snippet: 1. First, check `Gemfile.lock` for the exact installed version (look for `rails (x.y.z)`)
2. If not found, check `Gemfile` for the version constraint
This returns the latest stable version tag (e.g., `v8.0.1`). Strip the 'v' prefix for comparison.
If `package.json` exists, check for these Rails-related packages:
| `@hotwired/turbo-rails` | Turbo Drive/Frames/Streams | Should match Rails version era |
| `@hotwired/stimulus` | Stimulus JS framework | Generally stable across Rails versions |
| `@rails/actioncable` | WebSocket support | Should match Rails version |
| `@rails/activestorage` | Direct uploads | Should match Rails version |
| `@rails/actiontext` | Rich text editing | Should match Rails version |
| `@rails/request.js` | Rails UJS replacement | Should match Rails version era |
If the app uses importmap-rails, check `config/importmap.rb` for pinned versions:
- Run `npm update @rails/actioncable @rails/activestorage` to match Rails version
6. **DO NOT run `rails app:update` directly** - use the selective merge process below
**IMPORTANT:** Do NOT run `rails app:update` as it overwrites files without considering local custom
| **Unchanged locally** | Safe to overwrite | `public/404.html` (if not customized) |
3. Once all defaults are enabled and tested, update `config/application.rb`:
- If `gh` CLI is not authenticated, instruct the user to run `gh auth login`

content.value_statement: Rails upgrades can break configuration, dependencies, and local customizations. This skill guides Codex, Claude, or Claude Code through assessment, documentation review, and selective merge planning.
actual_capabilities: Verifies whether a workspace appears to be a Rails app using Gemfile and config files.
Extracts the current Rails version from Gemfile.lock or Gemfile.
Queries public Rails release data and compares current and target versions.
Reviews Rails upgrade guides and railsdiff output for target-version changes.
Checks related JavaScript packages and importmap pins for version alignment.
Produces upgrade summaries, complexity ratings, and selective merge plans.
limitations: Requires local project files and installed tools such as gh, bundle, npm, or Rails commands.
Public release data and upgrade guides may change after the assessment.
Cannot guarantee application compatibility without tests and custom code review.
Commands that update dependencies, migrations, or files should require explicit user approval.

use_cases.title: Assess an Upgrade Path
use_cases.description: Identify current and target versions, breaking changes, and estimated complexity before changing dependencies.

use_cases.title: Review Configuration Changes
use_cases.description: Compare Rails defaults with local customizations and decide which files need manual merge.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Dependency Updates
use_cases.description: Check related JavaScript packages and plan update steps for CI or release branches.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Rails Version
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify this workspace is a Rails app, identify the current Rails version, and stop before running update commands.

prompt_templates.title: Create Upgrade Summary
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess upgrading this Rails app to the latest stable Rails release. Include version jump, major risks, docs to review, and test priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Build Selective Merge Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this app's customized config, bin, and public files against Rails defaults for the target version. List safe updates and manual merges.

prompt_templates.title: Guide a Controlled Upgrade
prompt_templates.prompt: After I approve each step, help update Rails, related JavaScript packages, migrations, and framework defaults. Show commands before running them.

output_examples.input: User asks for a Rails 7.1 to Rails 8.0 assessment.
output_examples.output: A report with current and target versions, upgrade size, guide sections to review, dependency concerns, and a staged test plan.

output_examples.input: User asks whether the Rails update task can be run directly.
output_examples.output: A selective merge plan that separates new files, safe overwrites, locally customized files, and items to skip.

output_examples.input: User asks about Rails-related JavaScript dependencies.
output_examples.output: A dependency summary with package manager status, package alignment, update recommendations, and validation steps.

best_practices: Start by confirming the project is a Rails app and reading existing version files.
Ask for approval before commands that update dependencies, create files, or run migrations.
Review deprecation warnings and run tests after each meaningful change.
anti_patterns: Running broad update commands before understanding local customizations.
Treating railsdiff output as a complete replacement for project-specific review.
Skipping JavaScript packages that ship with Rails features.

faq.question: Does this skill perform the full Rails upgrade automatically?
faq.answer: No. It creates an assessment and can guide execution only after user approval.

faq.question: Which Rails versions does it support?
faq.answer: It is version-agnostic and compares the app version with current public Rails releases.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: Yes, for current release information, Rails guides, railsdiff data, and package versions.

faq.question: Can it protect local customizations?
faq.answer: It is designed to identify customized files and recommend selective merges before overwrites.

faq.question: Does it update JavaScript dependencies?
faq.answer: It can check and plan updates for Rails-related JavaScript packages and importmap pins.

faq.question: What should users prepare first?
faq.answer: Users should start from a clean git state and have tests available before upgrade execution.
